controls.description: Return the number of display heads for a subdevice; flags select the client's usable heads versus all heads. Input: subdevice and flags. Output: numHeads.

Detect connected displays using the requested detection flags (including cached/DDC paths). Input/output: display mask; also subdevice and retry time. This is connector discovery, not a GPU work submission.
Read hotplug state for a subdevice, including lid-state flags and the hotplug-after-EDID display mask.
Return the active display ID for a selected subdevice/head, with flags controlling client filtering.

Unresolved for Windows 580. Nouveau's historical r535 header assigns this number to GET_CONNECT_STATE with a 16-byte structure; Windows declares 8 bytes. r570 and OGKM 580 use 0x00730108 for connect state. The historical name is a candidate, not an established decoding of this call.

Opaque unresolved control. No semantic definition recovered in the searched sources; inputs, outputs, units and state effects remain unresolved. The observed length/status and Linux occurrences do not justify inventing a response or treating it as a no-op.
Add or remove a display from VRR display information using subdevice, display ID and an addition/removal boolean. This updates display state rather than querying a generic capability mask.
Query connector metadata for a display: DDC partners, connector count and per-connector index/type/location, plus platform information. Inputs select subdevice/display and query flags.

Candidate HDCP-state query from newer OGKM 595: subdevice/display select the target and flags report protection state, including HDCP 2.2. Published and captured lengths both equal 12 bytes; this does not prove all 580 semantics identical.

Candidate HDCP control from newer OGKM 595: command/flags drive authentication or link/topology handling. The 595 parameter structure is 2608 bytes versus 2600 declared by Windows 580. Exact 580 field offsets and subcommand semantics remain unresolved; do not apply the newer structure verbatim.
Query output-resource information for a display: resource index/type, protocol, dithering/location and connection/boot-state metadata. It describes the display routing hardware.
Notify RM of a display transition using new-device mask, properties and start/end indication, allowing display changes to be coordinated.

Opaque unresolved control. No semantic definition recovered in the searched sources; inputs, outputs, units and state effects remain unresolved. The observed length/status and Linux occurrences do not justify inventing a response or treating it as a no-op.
Query digital flat-panel information and capability flags for a display, including supported UHBR modes.
Query DisplayPort dongle capability/attachment/type flags and maximum TMDS clock for a selected digital display.
Supply ELD audio capability bytes, buffer length and audio/control metadata for a display receiver. This configures display audio; it is not a CUDA channel command.
Update selected entries in RM's dynamic digital-panel cache: head, HDCP capability/status and receiver identifiers, with reset/update masks.
Enable or disable digital-display audio for a subdevice/display; disabling stops audio and timestamp packets on the corresponding path.
Assign serial output resources (SORs) to displays under crossbar/link constraints, exclusions and sharing flags. This is stateful display-resource allocation.

Perform a DisplayPort AUX or I2C-over-AUX transaction. Inputs include display, command, address and data/length; outputs include reply type and retry information. This is physical-display communication, not a safe generic passthrough primitive.
Perform DisplayPort link-control operations selected by command/data and flags, including training/link configuration. Error and retry-time fields describe the result.
Set DisplayPort audio-stream muting mode (off/on/automatic) for the selected display.
Read current DisplayPort link configuration: lane count, link bandwidth (including DP2 representation) and FEC state.
Configure a DisplayPort stream: head/SOR/link, SST/MST selection, blanking/color settings and bandwidth/time-slot/transfer-unit parameters. This changes stream state.

Opaque unresolved control. No semantic definition recovered in the searched sources; inputs, outputs, units and state effects remain unresolved. The observed length/status and Linux occurrences do not justify inventing a response or treating it as a no-op.
Program stereo and selected main-stream-attribute (MSA) properties using feature masks/values and stereo enable/phase flags, independently of the normal supervisor-interrupt handling.
Extended MSA-property control, including feature masks/values, caching until a modeset and debug/readback fields. Exact behavior is selected by its input flags.
Return device brand capability bits (for example Quadro/NVS/Titan categories), not the device's numeric chip identity.

For an input engine ID, return latency-buffer sizes: GPFIFO entries and pushbuffer entries (32-byte rows). OGKM includes a vGPU implementation that reads cached per-engine values; that does not establish a universal sizing formula.

Set a selected channel property. Inputs are channel handle, property selector and 64-bit value. Selectors include scheduling/context-related settings; identifying the command alone does not implement every property.
Set the device's default virtual address space using hVASpace, subject to ownership/lifecycle checks. The public symbol omits _CMD_, which is why the earlier narrower name search missed it.
Query GPU information through a count and fixed array of index/data pairs. Each index has its own semantics; matching this outer layout does not imply every Windows index is supported.

Promote/bind supplied engine-context resources for a selected client/channel using context-buffer descriptors, flags and routing information. This changes context state; it is also nested in four deferred requests here.
Query per-unit ECC state: support/enabled/scrub status, correctable and uncorrectable counters, plus aggregate fatal-poison/error indications. Flags and GR routing identify the requested context.
Read the version of a selected InfoROM object. Input is the object selector; output is its version data. A missing board object can legitimately return OBJECT_NOT_FOUND.
Read the InfoROM image version string. This describes board nonvolatile metadata rather than driver or GSP firmware version.
Query whether InfoROM ECC support exists. No parameter block; the return status carries the answer (including NOT_SUPPORTED).
Read chip identity details, including PCI device ID, chip SKU and VBIOS chip revision fields.
Read whether FECS context-switch hardware tracing is enabled for the selected GR route. The boolean is an output; this is GET, not the neighboring SET operation.
Request/update an internal performance boost with flags and duration. This changes boost policy; it is not simply a clock-frequency query.
Notify internal display handling that the ACPI subsystem is active. The public declaration has no parameter block; the source name establishes the notification, not a complete firmware algorithm.
Internal display pre-modeset notification, with no parameter block. Signals the phase before a mode transition; firmware-side details are not published here.
Internal display post-modeset notification, with no parameter block. Signals the phase after a mode transition; firmware-side details are not published here.
Set polling of selected RM user-shared-data fields, using a data mask and requested polling interval in milliseconds. It changes telemetry update policy.

Disable or alter scheduling for a list of client/channel handles, with scheduling-only, rewind and runlist-preemption options. This is stateful channel management, not evidence of the channel's pushbuffer contents.

Opaque unresolved control. No semantic definition recovered in the searched sources; inputs, outputs, units and state effects remain unresolved. The observed length/status and Linux occurrences do not justify inventing a response or treating it as a no-op.
Bind ZCULL context-switch storage to a client/channel using its GPU virtual address and ZCULL mode.

Bind graphics/compute preemption context resources: client/channel, flags, graphics/compute modes, GR route and memory addresses for the main/spill/pagepool/beta/RTV and context-pool/control buffers. Resource sizes and correct state transitions still need implementation.

Query framebuffer/memory information via a count and index/data array. Different indices request different facts; the original Windows run exposed an unsupported index despite the known outer command.
Read offlined memory pages and associated source/status information. This reports memory retirement, not the ordinary GPU page-table mappings of an application.
Read remapped memory-row records and pending/failure flags. These are board reliability/remapping records, not a virtual-memory map operation.
Read the row-remapper histogram: bank counts grouped by remaining remapping capacity/usage. Values depend on hardware support and current board state.
Query InfoROM support/state for DRAM encryption. The returned enum distinguishes supported configurations and absent support; NOT_SUPPORTED is a legitimate result on some boards.
Read selected PCIe error/event counters, selected by counter mask. Returned telemetry must reflect the applicable link and hardware.
Read selected PCIe utilization counters, such as transmitted/received traffic and link-state residency, through a selection mask and returned counter fields.
Query bus information via a count and index/data array. Index-specific meaning matters; the earlier Windows failure included an unsupported index in this otherwise known command.
Query PCIe requester atomic-operation capabilities for a selected capability type and, where relevant, peer PCI address. Returns a capability bitmask.
Read PCIe completer atomic-operation capability bits.
Return the required copy-engine fault-method-buffer size in bytes, used when allocating channel fault-handling resources.
Query NVLink platform-placement metadata: GUIDs and rack/slot/node/compute placement. This is topology information, not an NVLink transfer submission.
Read client-visible ECC counters for supported memory/hardware units. Which counters are meaningful depends on the device's ECC capabilities.
Read volatile SRAM/DRAM error counts, including SRAM parity/SECDED and DRAM correctable/uncorrectable totals. These are telemetry since the relevant reset interval.
Read whether TPC or channel repair is pending, as two boolean status fields.

Register a deferred API call: target handle, nested command, flags and client/device VA-space handles surround a payload union. Here it contains INITIALIZE_CTX or PROMOTE_CTX. Wrapper success means acceptance; later deferred execution/completion is a separate event.
Query the last InfoROM black-box flush timestamp and duration in microseconds. NOT_READY can mean no flush yet; NOT_SUPPORTED can mean the board lacks the feature.

Pin/reserve page-directory coverage and mirror client page-table levels in server RM. Inputs describe the subdevice, VA interval, page size and per-level physical address/size/aperture/shift. This publishes address-space state, not a general data copy.
Schedule or deschedule a channel group (TSG) using bEnable, bSkipSubmit and bSkipEnable. This changes enable/runlist state; it does not contain GPU methods.
Set a channel group's timeslice in microseconds. Hardware may round the value down; the change is immediate and can force the channel off the GPU.

Promote fault-method-buffer descriptors for the channel group/runqueues, including memory/aperture/address information. This is context-resource setup; zero-sized descriptors can be used for teardown as specified by the SDK.
Schedule or deschedule a GPFIFO channel using bEnable, bSkipSubmit and bSkipEnable. This changes enable/runlist state; it does not contain the GPU methods fetched from the ring.

Query display-channel state for a hardware class/instance, including whether methods remain pending. This allows mode validation after methods propagate without itself committing an armed display state.

Validate whether a proposed display mode is possible using the supplied head/window/timing configuration and resource constraints. This asks about display assembly state; it is not a graphics-engine kernel launch.
